w:r.w:t: Moodify is an intelligent mobile application that detects the emotional state of a user through facial expression recognition or manual mood selection, and recommends a curated music playlist accordingly. The application bridges affective computing and music therapy by leveraging real-time camera-based emotion detection powered by machine learning, integrated with a robust music recommendation engine.

The system captures facial features, classifies them into one of several emotion categories (Happy, Sad, Angry, Relaxed, Energetic, etc.), and maps those emotions to genre-specific or mood-tagged music libraries. Users can also manually select their mood when camera access is unavailable. A daily mood history tracker enables users to review their emotional patterns over time. Moodify is designed to be intuitive, privacy-respecting, and genuinely useful for everyday emotional wellbeing.

Music has long been recognized as a powerful tool for emotional regulation. Scientific studies confirm that listening to music that matches or intentionally contrasts with one's current mood can reduce stress, improve concentration, and elevate overall wellbeing. However, manually searching for 'the right playlist' requires effort at precisely the moment when users are least motivated to exert it.

Advances in computer vision and deep learning now make it possible to detect human emotions from facial expressions in near real-time on consumer-grade mobile hardware. By combining emotion detection with automated music recommendation, Moodify removes the friction between 'how I feel' and 'what I should listen to'.
Current music streaming platforms require users to manually search or browse for mood-appropriate content. There is no seamless, automatic mechanism that:
Detects the user's current emotional state without manual input
Instantly surfaces a relevant, personalized playlist
Tracks emotional history for personal insight over time
Develop a mobile application capable of detecting emotions via facial expression analysis
Implement an alternative mood selection interface for accessibility
Design a music recommendation engine that maps detected emotions to curated playlists
Provide playlist creation, saving, and export functionality
Build a daily mood history dashboard with visualization
Ensure user privacy by performing emotion detection on-device
This project covers the end-to-end development of the Moodify Android/iOS application including:
Front-end UI built with React Native
On-device emotion detection using TensorFlow Lite / MediaPipe Face Mesh
Backend music catalogue and recommendation API
Local SQLite database for mood history
Integration with a music streaming API (Spotify / JioSaavn)
Existing music applications such as Spotify, Apple Music, and YouTube Music rely on:
Explicit user input: manual genre/mood selection or keyword search
Implicit behavioral data: listening history, skip rates, saves
Time/context signals: time of day, recently played
None of these systems actively detect the user's real-time emotional state via computer vision, creating a disconnect between current mood and recommended content.
Moodify introduces a camera-first, emotion-aware music experience:
Real-time facial emotion detection using the device front camera
Immediate playlist generation based on the detected mood
Fallback manual mood picker for users who prefer not to use the camera
Persistent mood history logged per session for longitudinal tracking
React Native + TFLite are mature, well-documented stacks. Emotion models (FER-2013 trained) achieve 65-70% accuracy on mobile.
Target users are smartphone owners aged 13-35 already comfortable with camera permissions.
Open-source ML models and free-tier APIs keep initial cost near zero.
MVP deliverable in 14 weeks with a 4-member team using Agile sprints.

Moodify follows a three-tier client-server architecture with an on-device ML layer:
React Native Mobile App (iOS & Android) — Camera UI, Mood Picker, Player, History Dashboard
Node.js / Express REST API — Recommendation Engine, Playlist Service, User Auth, Mood-to-Genre Mapper

The emotion detection module uses the device front camera to capture a frame every 2 seconds. MediaPipe Face Mesh extracts 468 facial landmarks, which are fed into a TensorFlow Lite classification model (based on FER-2013 dataset training). The output is one of 7 emotion labels with a confidence score. If confidence is below 55%, the system defaults to Neutral.

A rule-based and collaborative-filtering hybrid engine maps detected emotions to music attributes. Each emotion is associated with BPM ranges, energy levels, valence scores, and genre tags. These attributes are used to query the music API and rank results.

Users can save any generated playlist to their profile. Saved playlists are stored in the PostgreSQL backend. A one-tap Spotify export function uses the Spotify Web API to create the playlist directly in the user's Spotify account using OAuth 2.0 authorization.

Every detected or manually selected mood is logged with a Unix timestamp and stored in the device's local SQLite database. The History screen renders a bar chart (using React Native Charts) showing mood frequency across the past 7 or 30 days.
The primary actors in Moodify are the User and the System (backend). The main use cases are:
Detect Emotion — User allows camera; System classifies facial expression
Select Mood Manually — User taps a mood icon
View Playlist — System returns track list based on mood
Save Playlist — User saves playlist to profile
Export to Spotify — User exports playlist to Spotify account
View Mood History — User views emotion trends dashboard
Manage Account — User registers, logs in, updates preferences

The single process 'Moodify System' receives facial image / mood selection from the User and returns a playlist and mood data. It interacts with the Music API (Spotify / JioSaavn) and the Cloud Database for storing user and playlist data.

At Level 1, the system decomposes into four sub-processes: (1) Emotion Detection, (2) Recommendation Engine, (3) Playlist Manager, and (4) Mood History Logger. The camera frame flows into Emotion Detection; the emotion label flows into the Recommendation Engine which queries the Music API; the resulting tracks flow into the Playlist Manager; the mood event flows into the Mood History Logger which writes to the local SQLite store.

Has many Playlists; Has many MoodLogs
Belongs to User; Has many PlaylistTracks

Step 1 — Frame Capture: Grab front camera frame at 512x512 resolution
Step 2 — Face Detection: MediaPipe detects face bounding box
Step 4 — Feature Normalization: Coordinates normalized relative to face bounding box
Step 5 — Classification: Normalized features fed to TFLite model
Step 6 — Threshold Check: If max confidence < 0.55 → emit Neutral
Step 7 — Emit Label: Publish emotion label to recommendation engine

Moodify presents a novel approach to music discovery by making emotional state the primary signal for content recommendation. By combining on-device facial emotion recognition with a robust music mapping engine, the application removes the manual effort of finding mood-appropriate music while preserving user privacy.

The project demonstrates the practical application of affective computing, mobile machine learning, and RESTful API design in a cohesive consumer product. The modular architecture ensures that individual components — the emotion detector, the recommendation engine, and the history tracker — can be independently improved as technology evolves.

The successful implementation of Moodify will contribute to the growing field of emotionally intelligent applications and provide a tangible example of how machine learning can be deployed responsibly on mobile devices to improve everyday user experiences.
